correctness.rationale: For a stochastically monotone kernel, one-dimensional Wasserstein duality identifies the Lipschitz norm with the largest adjacent stationary-row-mean slope, simultaneously attained by the position potential. The fixed stationary marginal imposes an exact upper-tail rearrangement cap on each adjacent row-mean difference, and a two-block conditional expectation saturates every cut bound. The gradient generator of nearest-neighbor reversible heat is Metzler, making all its kernels stochastically monotone; positivity of all entries at positive time makes the upper-tail inequality strict. As one conductance vanishes and time diverges at the intermediate square-root scale, Duhamel comparison proves convergence to a two-block conditional expectation. No claim rests on numerical enumeration: 1,105 exact block cases, 720 independent semigroup/transport comparisons, 42 singular-limit diagnostics, and a nonmonotone boundary witness were successfully executed from the standalone code.

value.rationale: The exact optimum depends only on the invariant masses and locations, completely classifying the worst Lipschitz amplification permitted by a stationary law across every reversible nearest-neighbor heat dynamics on an arbitrary finite metric path. A sharp two-block metastable extremal mechanism and strict nonattainment at positive conductances follow. The stronger stationary-monotone variational theorem isolates the structural principle behind the result, while the sharp uniform law grows as n/2, ruling out dimension-free stationary-only control. This directly informs stability and transport coefficients on ordered reversible networks rather than computing an artificial finite statistic.
